items.ownerBrief: SUB-QUESTION RAISED, NOT ANSWERED — 12.02.03 Q-04. What does the per-store board render while a delivery is `Held`? `Held` fires when a partner profile is suspended, a partner endpoint is down, or a WeJammin credential lapsed. The release has been scheduled and not sent. 12.02.03 D-06 commits the platform to honest attribution and to the specific words 'held, not lost'; 12.02 CX-02's synthesis notes go further — 'the release is not broken, the partner is unreachable, and those must not look the same to the artist'. But 12.03.02 owns the status object (CX-02) and its vocabulary, its legal-transitions table and 12.05.03 contain no `Held` at all, so the promise has nowhere to render. Two shapes, not equivalent. (A) A distinct `Held` row state: renders the promise directly; costs one new state plus its legal transitions and a decision about whether the overdue clock runs while held. (B) The treatment `Failed` already got: the row keeps its prior state — `Queued` before `signal-complete`, `Sent` after — and carries a reason qualifier; adds no state, but leaves 'held, not lost' as copy hanging off a state that does not mean it, on a board that is exception-first (12.03.02 D-01). One boundary is already fixed either way and does not need deciding: per 12.02 CX-02, the pinned profile governs an in-flight delivery to completion, so a suspension applies only to what has not yet started. This was left to the owner rather than fixed because it adds a state to another feature's ratified vocabulary and changes what the artist sees on the most-viewed screen in the domain — that is product behaviour, not a sweep. Owner: User, with 12.03.02. Deferred to `/create-prd`.
